3. Mathematical Methodology

Adds a squared L2 penalty on standardized slopes (unpenalized intercept) to stabilize ill-conditioned matrices and reduce estimator variance.

$$\min_{\beta_0 \in \mathbb{R},\, \boldsymbol{\beta} \in \mathbb{R}^p} \|\mathbf{y} - \beta_0\mathbf{1} - \tilde{\mathbf{X}}\boldsymbol{\beta}\|_2^2 + \alpha\|\boldsymbol{\beta}\|_2^2, \qquad \hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}_{\alpha} = (\tilde{\mathbf{X}}^\top \tilde{\mathbf{X}} + \alpha \mathbf{I}_p)^{-1}\tilde{\mathbf{X}}^\top \tilde{\mathbf{y}} \quad (\lambda \equiv \alpha)$$

Implementation Note: min_{beta0, beta} ||y - beta0 - X*beta||_2^2 + alpha * ||beta||_2^2 (intercept beta0 unpenalized)
CV-Selected Hyperparameter: \(\alpha^* = 2982.47\) over 60 grid points in \([0.0001, 1e+05]\).

7. Limitations and Conclusions

Facts & Interpretations

  • [Computed Fact] Held-out test performance (n=1235): R² = -0.1900, RMSE = 9.93 UPDRS points (Train R² = 0.1775, Train RMSE = 9.995 UPDRS points).
  • [Computed Fact] Largest standardized coefficients by magnitude: age (+2.577), PPE (+1.047), test_time (+0.7118).
  • [Computed Fact] GroupKFold(5, group=subject#) selected alpha = 2982 (CV RMSE = 10.68 UPDRS points, CV R² = -0.1629), matching closed-form SVD within 5.77e-15.
  • [Interpretation] L2 regularization trades controlled bias for variance reduction, shrinking the standardized L2 norm from 1131 (OLS) to 3.05 (ratio = 0.0027) and reducing effective degrees of freedom from 19 to 5.76.
  • [Computed Fact] Adding alpha*I stabilized the centered X^T X condition number from 5.9131e+08 to 18.96.

Assumptions & Limitations

  • [No Feature Elimination] Ridge shrinks coefficients smoothly toward zero via L2 regularization and never sets coefficients exactly to zero; all predictors remain in the model.
  • [Group Generalization] Evaluation tests unseen 'subject#' clusters without subject-specific random intercepts.
  • [Generalization Gap] Test R² (-0.1900) drops from Train R² (0.1775), indicating distribution shift or limited linear generalization.
  • [Linearity Assumption] Linear models assume additive linear relationships between standardized predictors and conditional target expectation.
